title: Transport: for a type family P over A and a path p from x to y there is a function from P(x) to P(y)

standard_prerequisites: Dependent type families P over A and the identity type of A with its reflexivity element.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
The identity function on a type and dependent product types.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, for every path p in x = y a function transporting elements of P(x) to elements of P(y).
Name the constructed function the transport of p.
proof_roadmap: Define the type family D over x, y, p by D(x, y, p) = (P(x) to P(y)): the goal family assigns to each path the type of functions from the fibre at x to the fibre at y.
Base case: for each x in A, the element d(x) = the identity function on P(x) inhabits D(x, x, refl x).
Apply the induction principle: the element J(D, d, x, y, p) inhabits D(x, y, p) = (P(x) to P(y)) for every path p; define the transport of p to be this element.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction whose base case is the identity function; the subtlety is that the goal family lives in function types between the fibres, not in an identity type.
